introduction.title: Makerkit Loop
introduction.overview: A local, document-first workspace for PRDs that works alongside the user’s own coding agent. The user plans and builds by talking to their agent; Loop is where they read the plan, adjust it, follow progress and approve finished stories.

problemStatement.problem: Building with coding agents happens in a chat. The plan, what is done, what is next and what needs review are scattered across messages, so people lose track, agents drift out of scope, and non-technical builders cannot follow along.
problemStatement.marketOpportunity: Free, MIT-licensed tool that demonstrates the Makerkit Loop workflow (Plan → Build → Review → Ship) in videos and leads to the Makerkit kits.
targetUsers: Developers building SaaS products with a coding agent
Non-technical founders building with a coding agent

solutionOverview.description: Started with npx inside a project. It reads and edits the PRDs in .prds through @makerkit/prd, shows each PRD as a readable document with a plan check, shows stories on a board, tells the user what to ask their agent next, and lets them approve or send back stories the agent has finished.
keyFeatures: PRD document view with inline edits
Approve or send back a story
successMetrics: A user goes from an empty project to a first approved story without leaving the Loop + agent flow
The Makerkit Loop itself is built story by story with Loop

nonGoals: Replacing the user’s agent: no chat UI, no running or steering agents, no AI features of its own
Anything hosted: accounts, sync, sharing links or a cloud workspace
Kit management (env vars, translations, emails, database tools, plugins, kit updates)
A desktop shell (Tauri or Electron), auto-updates or code signing
outOfScope: Full diff review and an embedded live preview (the kits’ Dev Tools app covers these)
A cloud Supabase setup path; Docker stays required for kits
assumptions: Users already have a coding agent that supports MCP (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor)
PRDs live in the project repository and are shared through git

risks.description: A malicious page in another tab, or a DNS-rebinding site, reads or edits the project's PRDs through Loop's localhost server.
risks.mitigation: Session token on every request, Host and Origin checks against the server's own port, HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, frame-ancestors none; covered by request-guard tests.

risks.description: Loop and the agent write the same PRD at the same time and one silently overwrites the other, so the plan no longer matches what was agreed.
risks.mitigation: Every Loop write carries the revision it was based on; PrdService rejects stale writes and Loop reloads and tells the user.

risks.description: A PRD with hostile Markdown (script, javascript: links, images outside the project) runs code or leaks data when opened in Loop.
risks.mitigation: Markdown rendered without raw HTML, http(s) links only, images only from the PRD's attachments folder with symlinks resolved, SVG served with a sandbox CSP.

risks.description: The PRD format in @makerkit/prd changes and Loop shows stale or broken sections, or an older Loop drops fields written by a newer agent.
risks.mitigation: Loop reads PRDs only through PrdService; normalizePrd keeps unknown top-level fields; release Loop and @makerkit/prd together and pin the version.

risks.description: Users never connect their agent (MCP setup fails or is confusing), so Loop shows plans nobody builds and they abandon it.
risks.mitigation: Connect your agent (US010) checks the connection, and every view shows the exact instruction to give the agent.

risks.description: Approving a story commits unrelated work in progress, or a story is approved while the project checks fail.
risks.mitigation: Approval shows the files changed and the check results, and completion goes through PrdService's completion check; decide what is committed before building US009.

userStories.title: Secure local server
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to know that only Loop’s own page can talk to its local server so that other websites open in my browser cannot read or change my project
userStories.businessValue: other websites open in my browser cannot read or change my project
acceptanceCriteria: A random session token is generated at launch and required on every server request
Requests with a Host other than 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port> are rejected
Requests with a foreign Origin are rejected
Read-only requests are protected too
testSeams: request guard used by every server function

whatsNew: `pnpm dev` prints an "Open Loop" link with a session token. Opening it lets you in; opening Loop without it shows "Open Loop from the link in your terminal."
Other websites in your browser can't read or change anything through Loop's server: requests from another site, another port or another host name are refused, read-only ones included.
technicalNotes: Guard logic is pure and unit-tested: src/lib/security/request-guard.ts (+ .test.ts, 33 tests, `pnpm test` with vitest). It checks Host (127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port>, port from config, never from request.url), then Origin (if present, must match exactly; 'null' rejected), then the token.

Applied to every request via global request middleware in src/start.ts. Adding start.ts replaces Start's default CSRF middleware; the guard covers that job. Do not add a second check in function middleware: SSR calls server functions in-process with no headers.

Server functions need the `x-loop-session` header (cookie not accepted). Pages need the HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie `loop_session_<port>`, set by visiting `/?token=...`, which redirects to the same URL without the token.

The client gets the token from `<meta name="loop-session">`, rendered in __root.tsx head through the isomorphic getPageSessionToken (src/lib/security/page-session-token.ts). createStart's serverFns.fetch adds the header. The token is never stored in a JS-readable cookie, because cookies aren't port-scoped.

Token and port come from LOOP_SESSION_TOKEN and LOOP_PORT (falling back to NITRO_PORT, PORT, then 3000), read in src/lib/security/session.server.ts. In dev, the loop-session plugin in vite.config.ts sets them in the `config` hook, which must run before Nitro's dev worker copies process.env. Setting them in configResolved was too late. Dev binds 127.0.0.1:3000 with strictPort.

For US011 (npx launcher): set LOOP_SESSION_TOKEN, LOOP_PORT/PORT and HOST=127.0.0.1 before starting .output/server/index.mjs, then open the ?token= URL. Without the env var, the prod server generates a token lazily and logs the URL only on the first request.

Verified with curl against the prod build. A GET server function returns 403 without the token, with a foreign Host and with a foreign Origin, and 200 with the token. Pages: 403, then 302 with Set-Cookie, then 200. Static /assets are served by Nitro without the guard (built JS/CSS only). Not verified in a real browser (Chrome extension unavailable): that the page's server function calls send the header from the meta tag.

userStories.notes: Approved by the user in chat ("commit and continue"); committed as 6ec45e6.

userStories.title: List the project’s PRDs
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to see the PRDs in my project’s .prds folder so that I can pick the plan I am working on
userStories.businessValue: I can pick the plan I am working on
acceptanceCriteria: Lists each PRD with its title, progress and story counts
With no .prds folder, explains how to start a PRD with the agent (shape_prd)
Unreadable files are shown as warnings, not errors
The project root is resolved on the server; paths from the browser are never trusted

whatsNew: Opening Loop now shows the project's PRDs: title, file name, last update, a progress bar, "X of Y stories completed" and a badge for blocked stories.
In a project with no PRDs, Loop explains how to start one with the agent's shape_prd prompt and offers a "Copy instruction" button.
PRD files that can't be read (e.g. broken JSON) appear as a warning above the list; the other PRDs still show.
technicalNotes: @makerkit/prd is linked as `link:../makerkit/packages/prd/dist`. Linking the package root fails because its exports point at the built files in dist/. Rebuild the package after changing it.

src/lib/prds/project.server.ts resolves the project root once, from LOOP_PROJECT_ROOT (for the US011 launcher) or process.cwd(), via realpath. It also holds the cached PrdService (getPrdService) and prdsDirExists. Future server functions should use getPrdService() and never accept paths from the browser.

PrdService.list() calls mkdir on .prds, so it creates the folder as a side effect. listProjectPrds (src/lib/prds/list-project-prds.ts, pure, tested against the real PrdService with in-memory deps) checks the folder first, so viewing Loop never creates .prds. Consider making list() read-only in @makerkit/prd.

The listPrds server function is in src/lib/prds/prds.functions.ts. It takes no input, so there is no Zod validator. The / route loads it; the route has pending (skeleton) and error (alert with Try again) components.
Progress and story counts come from the `progress` field stored in the PRD file, which PrdService keeps updated on writes. They are not recomputed on read.

Shared UI: src/components/copy-instruction.tsx (instruction text plus a "Copy instruction" button), reusable for the Ask your agent story (US008). PRD cards are not links yet; US003 adds the document page.

Verified on the prod build: this project lists makerkit-loop.json; an empty dir shows the empty state and .prds is not created; a broken JSON file shows a warning plus the valid PRD. The listPrds RPC returns 403 without the session header.

userStories.notes: Approved by the user in chat ("continue"); committed in 3b70018.

userStories.title: Read a PRD as a document
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to read a PRD as a clean document so that I can review and share the plan before anything is built
userStories.businessValue: I can review and share the plan before anything is built
acceptanceCriteria: Shows overview, problem, solution, scope, glossary, decisions, risks and open questions
Shows the data model (entities and how they relate, in plain language) and the outside services with the credentials or environment variables each one needs
Renders Markdown in PRD text safely: raw HTML is not rendered, links open only for http(s) URLs, and images load only from the PRD’s attachments folder
Superseded decisions are marked as such
Readable on a phone-width screen

whatsNew: Click a PRD in the list to read it as a document: Overview, Problem, Solution, Scope, Data model, Outside services, Glossary, Decisions, Risks and Open questions. Empty sections say "Not written yet."

Formatting in PRD text (bold, lists, code, links) is displayed. Links open in a new tab, but only web (http/https) links are clickable. Images show only when they are files in the PRD's own folder (.prds/<prd name>/); any other image shows its description in brackets instead.
Superseded decisions are greyed out, struck through and labelled "Superseded". Risks show their severity, owner and mitigation.
Opening a PRD that doesn't exist shows "PRD not found" with a link back to all PRDs.
technicalNotes: The route is src/routes/prds/$filename.tsx. Its loader calls getPrd (src/lib/prds/prds.functions.ts), which validates input with PrdFilenameSchema (Zod), throws notFound() when the file is missing, and returns { filename, prd } without PrdService's absolute path. The loader also turns a malformed name into notFound client-side.

Section mapping: data model = technicalContracts.dataModels; outside services = technicalRequirements.integrationNeeds (this is where the shape_prd prompt records them). The components are in src/components/prds/prd-document.tsx and document-parts.tsx.

Safe Markdown is src/components/markdown.tsx (react-markdown + remark-gfm). skipHtml drops raw HTML; links render only for http(s) URLs (otherwise as a span); images go through resolveImageSrc. `inline` mode is for list items. The PRD file name comes from PrdFileProvider context. Tests are in markdown.test.tsx (renderToStaticMarkup); vitest now also picks up *.test.tsx.

Image rules are in src/lib/prds/prd-paths.ts: a src path is relative to `.prds/<name>/` (optionally prefixed `./` or `.prds/<name>/`) and maps to /attachments/<name>/<path>. Remote, data:, absolute and `..` paths are refused. isSafeRelativePath mirrors @makerkit/prd's assertSafeRelativePath, which the package doesn't export.

Attachment files are served by the server route src/routes/attachments/$folder/$.ts through serveAttachment (attachments.server.ts) and resolveAttachmentFile (attachment-file.ts, tested with real symlinks in a temp dir). The route serves only image types and resolves symlinks with realpath; it refuses a PRD folder that is itself a symlink and any file resolving outside the folder. Responses carry CSP sandbox + nosniff, so an SVG can't run script. Like everything else it is covered by the US001 request guard (cookie).
Added dependencies: react-markdown, remark-gfm, zod (v4).

Verified on the prod build with a demo PRD: all sections render; a script tag and a javascript: link are dropped; a remote image shows its alt text; the local image is served (200 image/png) and is 403 without the cookie; symlink, `..` and non-image paths get 404; nope.json and a malformed name show 'PRD not found'. Phone width: the layout is a single column (max-w-3xl, px-4) with overflow-wrap:anywhere, but it was not checked in a real browser.

userStories.notes: Approved by the user in chat ("yes").

userStories.title: Edit PRD sections inline
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to edit a section of the PRD where I read it so that I can fix the plan without asking the agent
userStories.businessValue: I can fix the plan without asking the agent
acceptanceCriteria: Edits go through update_prd_section rules and show validation errors inline
If the PRD changed elsewhere, the user is told and the latest version is loaded

whatsNew: Most parts of a PRD now have an Edit button: Overview (including the title), Problem, Solution, Non-goals, Out of scope, Assumptions, Data model, Outside services, Quality bar, Rollout, Measurement and Open questions. Lists are edited one item per line. Save writes the change into the PRD; Cancel discards it.
Mistakes are shown next to the field, e.g. "Title can't be empty.", and nothing is saved.

If the agent (or anyone else) changed the PRD while you were editing, your edit is not saved. Loop loads the latest version, shows it next to your changes and explains what happened. You can then save again on purpose or cancel.
Glossary, decisions, risks and stories are not editable here yet.
technicalNotes: @makerkit/prd change (in ~/Code/makerkit, NOT committed there): update_prd_section accepts an optional expectedRevision. PrdService.mutate rejects with the new exported PrdRevisionConflictError (code 'PRD_REVISION_CONFLICT') when the PRD's revision differs; the existing save-time check now uses the same error. Tests are in packages/prd/src/__tests__/planning.test.ts. dist was rebuilt; Loop links dist.
Why: the old check only compared a read and a write within one mutate call, so a browser edit based on an old read silently overwrote the agent's change to the same section.

Loop side: section specs are in src/lib/prds/section-edits.ts. Each editable block maps to exactly one update_prd_section section, so a save is one atomic write; Scope is three separate editors for that reason. readEditValues / buildSectionValue convert PRD values to and from form fields (lists are one item per line; '- ' bullets are stripped). parseSectionErrors maps PrdService's 'Invalid value for section' message to fields and handles both zod 3 and zod 4 wording. A test asserts that every spec builds a value PrdSectionValueSchemas accepts.

updatePrdSection server function (POST, Zod: filename, section limited to EDITABLE_SECTIONS, value unknown, expectedRevision). It delegates to updateSection (src/lib/prds/update-section.ts), which returns { status: saved | conflict | invalid } and throws anything else. It matches conflicts by error code, so @makerkit/prd isn't a runtime import in a client-reachable module. Tests use the real PrdService with in-memory deps (src/lib/prds/testing/memory-prd-deps.ts, shared with the US002 test).

UI: src/components/prds/section-editor.tsx (form; PrdEditProvider context with filename + prd) and editable-section.tsx (EditableSection h2 / EditableSubsection h3 with an Edit button). Success and conflict both call router.invalidate(), which also refreshes the plan check panel. After a conflict the editor keeps the draft, shows the latest saved view, and the next save is based on the latest revision.

Verified on the prod build by POSTing seroval-encoded bodies, as the client does. A save with the current revision is written (revision 0 to 1). A stale revision returns conflict and leaves the file unchanged. An empty title returns invalid with no write. A non-editable section and a bad filename are rejected by the validator; a missing token gets 403. Not verified in a browser: the form interaction itself (typing, Save, Cancel, the conflict display).

userStories.notes: Approved by the user in chat ("y").

userStories.title: Plan check panel
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to see what my plan is still missing so that I know what to fix before the build starts
userStories.businessValue: I know what to fix before the build starts
acceptanceCriteria: Shows required and recommended items from check_plan
Each item links to its section or stories
Shows whether the plan is ready to build

whatsNew: The top of each PRD page says whether the plan is "Ready to build" or "Not ready to build", and lists what the plan is still missing, split into Required and Recommended.
Each item links to the part of the document to fix ("Go to Scope", "Go to Rollout"...). Items about specific stories list those stories, each linking to the story.
The document now also shows the Quality bar (global acceptance criteria), the Stories (grouped by phase in build order, with status and acceptance criteria), Rollout and Measurement.
technicalNotes: The getPlanCheck server function (src/lib/prds/prds.functions.ts) calls PrdService.checkPlan with Zod-validated input and returns notFound for missing files. The /prds/$filename loader runs getPrd and getPlanCheck in parallel.

src/lib/prds/plan-check-targets.ts maps check_plan's `section` to a document anchor and storyIds to `story-<id>` anchors. Its test runs the real checkPlan on a sparse PRD and asserts that every section it reports has an anchor, so a new check_plan section with no anchor fails the test.

The panel is src/components/prds/plan-check-panel.tsx and uses plain hash links. Item messages come verbatim from @makerkit/prd and some mention field names (measurementPlan, testSeams). Plainer wording belongs in the package.

Added document sections: Quality bar, Stories (src/components/prds/document-stories.tsx; read-only, grouped by customPhases order, then 'Not in a phase'), Rollout, Measurement. Status badges show the raw status with spaces (e.g. 'in progress'); plainer status labels are still undecided. US006's board can link to the same story-<id> anchors or replace them.

Verified on the prod build: this project is 'Ready to build' with 3 recommended items; the demo PRD is 'Not ready' with 1 required + 6 recommended; a PRD with vague and blocked stories links US001/US002. In every case all panel links resolve to an element on the page.

userStories.notes: Approved by the user in chat ("ok continue").

userStories.title: Stories board
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to see the stories by status and phase so that I know what is done, in progress, waiting and next
userStories.businessValue: I know what is done, in progress, waiting and next
acceptanceCriteria: Columns by status, stories grouped by phase in build order
The next ready story is highlighted; waiting stories show what they wait for
Opening a story shows its acceptance criteria, test seams and log, including any deviations from the plan the agent recorded

whatsNew: Each PRD now has two tabs: Document and Stories.

Stories shows a board with a column per status (Not started, In progress, Review, Completed; Research and Blocked appear only when used). Inside each column, stories are grouped by phase in build order.
The next story to build is highlighted with a "Next" badge, and a line above the board names it (or says why nothing is ready). Stories that can't start yet say what they're waiting for.

Click a story to open its details in a side panel: acceptance criteria, where it is tested, what it depends on (with each dependency's status), notes, check results and its log, newest first. Deviations from the plan are called out at the top of each log entry. The panel has its own link (…/stories?story=US001).
Stories in the Document tab now link to their details on the board.
technicalNotes: Route: src/routes/prds/$filename_.stories.tsx. The `_` un-nests it from the document route, so the path is /prds/$filename/stories. Its loader calls getPrd and the new getNextStory server function (prds.functions.ts; PrdService.getNextStory) in parallel. validateSearch accepts `story` only if it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/.

Pure board model in src/lib/prds/story-board.ts: buildStoryBoard(prd, nextStory) and groupStoriesByPhase (shared with the document's Stories section; it replaced that component's private copy). STATUS_LABELS holds the status display names; they are just the status words, not new vocabulary. Tests are in story-board.test.ts, using the package's pickNextStory.
Shared page chrome is in src/components/prds/prd-page.tsx (layout with a `wide` option, header with Document/Stories tabs, pending/error/not-found states, prdPageTitle). Both PRD routes use it.

Components: src/components/stories/story-board.tsx (columns, cards, NextStorySummary) and story-details.tsx (sheet content). Story links use resetScroll={false} so opening a story keeps the board's scroll position. story-details.test.tsx renders inside an open Sheet with a minimal in-memory router (Links need a router context).
The details sheet renders in a portal, so it's client-only. It is covered by the component test, not by the SSR check. Log times are shown in UTC to avoid hydration mismatches.
US008 (Ask your agent) and US009 (Approve) can add their actions to StoryDetails; the review column is where approval will start.

Verified on the prod build against this project's PRD: 200 for the board and for ?story=US001; 4 columns; Stories tab active; next = US011 with exactly one Next badge; a missing PRD shows 'PRD not found'; an invalid ?story value is ignored. The sheet interaction itself was not checked in a browser.

userStories.notes: Approved by the user in chat ("commit this").

userStories.title: Live updates from the agent
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to see changes the agent makes to the PRD as they happen so that I can follow progress without reloading
userStories.businessValue: I can follow progress without reloading
acceptanceCriteria: Changes to .prds appear in the open view within two seconds
Watching stops when no browser is connected

whatsNew: Changes the agent makes to a PRD (a story moved, a log written, a section updated) now appear in the open page by themselves, without reloading.
The top bar shows "Live" while Loop is receiving changes, and "Reconnecting…" if the connection drops.
technicalNotes: Commit on main after 3013738. Watcher: src/lib/live/prds-watcher.ts (pure, injected fs.watch and timers, unit tested: watches only while subscribed, debounces 150ms, waits for .prds to be created, stops if everyone left during start-up). Node wiring: src/lib/live/watcher.server.ts (one instance on globalThis, recursive fs.watch).

Route src/routes/api/events.ts: text/event-stream with retry 2000 and a 20s heartbeat; protected by the request guard (cookie, Host, Origin) like every route; unsubscribes on request abort and stream cancel.
Client: src/hooks/use-live-updates.ts calls router.invalidate() 100ms after a burst; mounted in the root layout. Editors keep their drafts and still save against the revision they started from.

Verified on the prod build: /api/events is 403 without the cookie and with a foreign Origin; a PrdService write reached the stream in ~0.26s; in a headless browser the board moved US002 into Blocked 378ms after an outside status change, without reloading the page.

userStories.title: Ask your agent
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to see exactly what to ask my agent next so that I never have to guess the next step
userStories.businessValue: I never have to guess the next step
acceptanceCriteria: No PRD yet: suggests starting with shape_prd
A ready story: suggests implementing it with implement_story
A story in review: points to the approve view instead
The instruction can be copied with one click

whatsNew: Every PRD page has an "Ask your agent" card with the exact instruction to give your agent next, and a Copy instruction button.

It follows where the work stands: a story waiting for your review links to it; a story in progress says whether your agent is probably still working (project files changed recently); a story you sent back asks the agent to address your notes; an unready plan asks to finish it with shape_prd; otherwise it names the next story to implement.
With no PRD yet, the PRD list still suggests starting with shape_prd.
technicalNotes: Pure logic: src/lib/agent/next-step.ts (nextStep with tests covering each case). Activity signal: src/lib/agent/activity.ts (newest mtime of uncommitted files outside .prds, via git status) and getProjectActivity in src/lib/stories/stories.functions.ts; polled every 15s in the browser only while a story is in progress, so server and client render the same.
UI: src/components/agent/ask-your-agent.tsx; replaces NextStorySummary on the board and sits under "Waiting on you" on the document. The PRD list's empty state uses the same START_INSTRUCTION.

Loop cannot know whether the agent is running; recent file changes are a heuristic (5 minutes = "probably working"). The user raised this question; the card no longer tells them to continue a story the agent is likely still on.

Instructions name the MCP prompts (implement_story, shape_prd) and mention slash commands. Verified with screenshots on the prod build for the in-progress and next-story cases; the copy button itself was not clicked in a browser.

userStories.title: Approve or send back a story
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to approve a finished story or send it back with notes so that only work I have checked counts as done
userStories.businessValue: only work I have checked counts as done
acceptanceCriteria: Shows the story log, the files changed and the result of the project checks
Deviations from the plan recorded in the story log are shown first, before the rest of the log; with none, it says so
Approve marks the story completed (the checks must pass) and commits the changes with the story id
Send back records my notes on the story for the agent to read

whatsNew: A story in review opens with a Review block: deviations from the plan first (or "No deviations recorded"), the changed files to commit with checkboxes, the commit message and a Run checks button.
Approve story runs the project checks, marks the story completed and commits the ticked files together with the PRD file; unticked changes stay exactly as they are.
If the commit fails (e.g. a pre-commit hook), the story is completed and Loop says it was not committed, with a Commit again button.
Send back records your notes at the top of the story's notes and returns it to in progress for the agent.
Every story has a ⋯ menu (on the board card and in the panel) to move it to Blocked, Research or back to Not started.
technicalNotes: Deviation: EC012 says "respect the user changes". Implemented as: every changed file starts ticked, the user unticks unrelated work, and Loop never stages, unstages or discards anything it was not asked to commit (git commit -- <paths> leaves the rest of the index as is). Confirm or change the default (e.g. untick files that were already staged).

Git: src/lib/git/ (git-status.ts -z parser, git.ts state/commit with --literal-pathspecs, run-command.server.ts execFile with timeout, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, sanitize.ts). Tests run against real temp repos isolated from global git config.

Review: src/lib/stories/review.ts (approve, commitAgain, sendBack, move; checks git blockers before completing so a story is never completed uncommitted because git was locked/conflicted), moves.ts (manual moves, server-enforced), review.server.ts, stories.functions.ts (Zod-validated). UI: src/components/stories/story-review.tsx and move-story-menu.tsx.

@makerkit/prd (uncommitted): update_story_status takes expectedRevision, checked before the slow checks; implement_story finishes an in-progress story first and reads its notes first; createScriptVerifier passes with no checks when there is no package.json (found by the end-to-end test).

Verified in a headless browser on a temp git project: approving committed the story's files with message "US002: Stop reminders when the invoice is paid" and marked it completed. Send back and the move menu are covered by tests but were not clicked in a browser.

userStories.title: Connect your agent
userStories.userStory: As a Loop user, I want to connect the PRD tools to the agent I already use so that my agent can plan and build with the PRD
userStories.businessValue: my agent can plan and build with the PRD
acceptanceCriteria: Detects Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
Shows and applies the configuration that adds the PRD MCP server (the kit’s own server inside a kit)
Confirms the connection works
testSeams: agent detection and config writer services

whatsNew: "Connect your agent" in the top bar opens a page that shows which agents are installed (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) and whether this project already gives them the PRD tools.
For Claude Code and OpenCode, one click adds the PRD server to the project's .mcp.json or opencode.json; for Codex, Loop shows the codex mcp add command to copy.
Inside a Makerkit kit, Loop connects the kit's own MCP server, which already includes the PRD tools.
Check the connection starts the server the way your agent would and confirms the PRD tools answer.
technicalNotes: Deviation: "Confirms the connection works" is done by starting the configured server and running the MCP handshake (initialize + tools/list), not by asking the agent: Loop never talks to the agent. It confirms the setup, not that the agent loaded it.

Deviation: Codex is configured by a copyable command rather than by Loop, because its MCP config is global (~/.codex/config.toml) and Loop only writes inside the project. Agent detection checks PATH for the CLIs without running them.

Pure logic: src/lib/agents/agents.ts (chooseServer, detectAgents, applyConfig, isPrdServer) and probe.ts (probeServer, configuredServer) with tests, one against the real local prd-mcp server. customPhases.name: Foundation
customPhases.description: Open Loop from the terminal link and see the project's PRDs.

customPhases.name: Document
customPhases.description: Open a PRD, read it as a document, edit a section and see what the plan is still missing.

customPhases.name: Stories
customPhases.description: See the stories by status and phase update live while the agent works, and copy what to ask the agent next.

customPhases.name: Review
customPhases.description: Review a story the agent finished, with its deviations, changed files and checks, then approve it or send it back.

customPhases.name: Setup
customPhases.description: Run npx @makerkit/loop in a new project and connect the agent from Loop.

customPhases.name: Plan quality
customPhases.description: Make the plan hard to get wrong before the build: a document that shows what is missing, edge cases, security and design, questions the user answers in place. Ends with a PRD a person can review, answer and approve in Loop.

constraints: TanStack Start on Node, bound to 127.0.0.1
PRD format and rules come from @makerkit/prd; changes to them are made there, with tests
integrationNeeds: PRD tools: @makerkit/prd (PrdService) inside Loop, and the PRD MCP server in the user's agent (the kit's own server inside a kit, otherwise @makerkit/prd-mcp). No credentials.
Git: the git CLI in the project, for changed files and the approval commit. No credentials.
Coding agent: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Cursor, configured by the user. Loop needs no API keys.
complianceRequirements: Nothing leaves the user's machine: no accounts, telemetry, analytics or remote fonts and scripts.
PRDs can contain confidential product plans and customer details: they stay in the repository and are shared only through git.
The session token is never written to disk, logs, URLs after launch, or a cookie that page scripts can read.

dataModels: Project: the folder Loop was started in. Resolved once on the server; holds one .prds folder.
PRD: one JSON file in .prds, read and written only through PrdService. Has many phases, stories, decisions and glossary terms.
Phase: an ordered group of stories in one PRD, built in order.
Story: one slice of work in a PRD. Belongs to at most one phase; may depend on other stories; has a status and a list of story log entries.
Story log entry: written by the agent when it finishes a session on a story: what is new, technical notes, and deviations from the plan.
Session token: random value created at launch. Not stored on disk; required on every request to Loop's server.
permissions: Only the page Loop opened can call its server: every request needs the session token created at launch; other websites, other localhost ports and other host names are refused, read-only requests included.
Whoever holds the launch link can read and change every PRD in the project. There are no roles or accounts; the link must not be shared or logged.
Loop reads and writes only inside the project it was started in: the .prds folder and each PRD's attachments folder. Paths sent by the browser are never trusted.
The agent changes PRDs only through the PRD MCP tools; Loop only through PrdService. Neither edits .prds files by hand.
A story becomes completed only when a person approves it in Loop; the agent can move it to review at most.

global: Every server request is rejected without the session token or with a foreign Host or Origin.
Loop never writes .prds files directly; every change goes through PrdService.
A write rejected by the revision check tells the user the PRD changed elsewhere and reloads it.
Empty, loading and error states are handled on every view.
qualityStandards: Cut scope before cutting quality on the main flow.

decisionLog.decision: Open a PRD as a readable document and see exactly what to ask their agent next.
decisionLog.rationale: Answers the open question: What is the one thing a first user must be able to do?

decisionLog.decision: We build Loop itself with Loop: every story goes from ready to approved through the app and the PRD server.
decisionLog.rationale: Answers the open question: How will we know it works (a number or a behaviour we can observe)?

decisionLog.decision: Loop is a companion to the user’s coding agent; it never runs, drives or chats with agents.
decisionLog.rationale: We cannot replace the agents people already use and pay for, and wrapping them means chasing protocol changes.

decisionLog.decision: Loop is a localhost web app started with npx, not a desktop app.
decisionLog.rationale: The earlier Tauri attempt stalled on shell allow-lists and scope; prerequisites, not the shell, are the real barrier for new users.

decisionLog.decision: The PRD files in .prds are the only state, and Loop writes them through PrdService.
decisionLog.rationale: The agent (through MCP) and Loop then share the same rules, including the revision check that stops either from overwriting the other.

decisionLog.decision: A PRD opens as a readable document; the stories board is one view of it.
decisionLog.rationale: Anyone, technical or not, can review the plan before the build starts.

decisionLog.decision: One story at a time, in the user’s current checkout.
decisionLog.rationale: Keeps review simple and avoids merge handling in the first version.

decisionLog.decision: Keep one JSON file per PRD; do not split it into per-story or per-phase files.
decisionLog.rationale: get_story already gives the agent a scoped slice, and story logs already carry context between sessions. One file keeps a single revision counter, saves that never land half-written, and one file for Loop to watch. Revisit only if story logs make files large.

decisionLog.decision: Agents record deviations from the plan in the story log, and Loop shows them first in the approve view.
decisionLog.rationale: What changed versus the plan is what the person approving needs to judge; burying it in technical notes hides it. Borrowed from Builder Methods' PRD Creator milestone logs.

decisionLog.decision: Neutral tool look: shadcn on Base UI with Inter, a warm off-white background, white surfaces, one blue accent for what is next, and one colour per story status.
decisionLog.rationale: Loop sits next to the user's own tools for long sessions; a quiet, document-first look keeps attention on the plan. Chosen by the user over a warm-document or brand look.

decisionLog.decision: Layout: a slim top bar (Loop, project name), a PRD header with Document and Stories tabs, a sticky table of contents with section status on the document, and story details in a side panel linked by ?story=.
decisionLog.rationale: Keeps the plan, its gaps and the board one click apart without a sidebar app; the side panel keeps the board in view and gives every story a shareable link.
Answers Q003: Should there be an Auto-continue switch, and is it off by default?
Answers Q004: When a story is sent back, which status does it return to?

glossary.definition: The product requirements document in .prds that the user and their agent plan and build from.
One thin slice of work from a PRD that a person can try once it is done.
An ordered group of stories, built in order.
The hand-off an agent writes on a story: what is new for a person to try, notes for the next agent, and any deviations from the plan.
The checklist of what a PRD is still missing, from check_plan.
The user’s own coding agent, such as Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode.

A place where the agent's work departed from the PRD (a criterion changed or skipped, extra scope, a different approach), recorded in the story log with the reason, for the person approving the story.

edgeCases.case: Another website open in the browser calls Loop's server (fetch, form post, image or script tag)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Refused with 403 before any work; nothing about the project is returned.

edgeCases.case: A DNS-rebinding site (attacker domain resolving to 127.0.0.1) calls Loop's server
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Refused because the Host header is not 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port>.

edgeCases.case: Loop is opened without the launch link, or with a wrong token
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: 403 page that says to open Loop from the link in the terminal; no PRD data shown.

edgeCases.case: A .prds file is broken JSON or hand-edited into an invalid shape
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Listed as a warning naming the file; the other PRDs still show.
Empty state explaining how to start a PRD with the agent; the folder is not created by viewing.

edgeCases.case: PRD text contains <script>, raw HTML or javascript: links
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Nothing runs: HTML is dropped and only http(s) links are clickable.

edgeCases.case: A Markdown image points outside the PRD's folder, at a remote URL, or through a symlink
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The image is not loaded; its alt text is shown instead.

edgeCases.case: The agent changes the PRD while the user is editing a section
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The edit is not saved; the latest version is loaded and shown next to the user's changes with an explanation; saving again is a deliberate choice.

edgeCases.case: A section is saved with invalid content (e.g. an empty title)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Nothing is written; the error is shown next to the field.

edgeCases.case: The agent moves a story to review while the board is open
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The board and the open story update without a reload.

edgeCases.case: The user approves a story while the project checks fail
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Approval is refused and the failing checks are shown; the story stays in review.

edgeCases.case: The user approves a story while the git working tree has changes unrelated to the story
Port 3000 is already in use when Loop starts
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: can Tanstack open a new port? not sure

edgeCases.case: npx @makerkit/loop is run in a folder that is not a project (no package.json and no git)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: it's normally okay, we only require a .prds folder

securityConsiderations: Bind the server to 127.0.0.1 only; never listen on other interfaces.
Every server function and server route checks the session token, Host and Origin, read-only ones included (see the request guard).
Validate every server function input with Zod; the browser is untrusted even on localhost.
PRD file names and attachment paths are checked before touching the disk, and files are resolved with realpath so symlinks cannot leave the PRD's folder.
Render PRD Markdown without raw HTML; links only for http(s); images only from the PRD's attachments folder; serve attachments with nosniff and a sandbox CSP.
Every write from Loop carries the PRD revision it was based on; a stale write is rejected, never forced.
Run git and other commands with argument arrays, never a shell string built from PRD text, file names or branch names.
Never log or display the session token, environment variables or secrets; error messages shown in the UI must not include absolute paths or stack traces.
Loop never frames other sites and cannot be framed (frame-ancestors none, X-Frame-Options DENY).
designGuidance: Every view has empty, loading and error states; an empty state says what to ask the agent next.
UI copy is literal and short; buttons say what they do ("Approve story", "Send back", "Copy instruction").
Use the shadcn components on Base UI already in src/components/ui; add new ones with the shadcn CLI, never by hand.
A story's status always uses the same colour and label everywhere (board, document, story panel).
Everything works at phone width with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll, except the board's columns.
Actions on a section (Edit, Mark as N/A) appear on hover or focus on desktop and are always visible on touch screens.
